related_questions.question: Which anticoagulant is preferred for atrial fibrillation?
related_questions.snippet: Both of these anti-clotting medications, rivaroxaban (Xarelto) and apixaban (Eliquis), are FDA-approved for preventing strokes in people with atrial fibrillation (afib). They both belong to a class of drugs known as direct oral anticoagulants, or DOACs.

related_questions.question: Why is aspirin not recommended for atrial fibrillation?

text_blocks.snippet: Aspirin is generally not recommended as the primary treatment for preventing strokes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AFib) because it is less effective than other anticoagulants and carries a similar risk of bleeding, according to the Oklahoma Heart Hospital. While aspirin may be used for other conditions, oral anticoagulants, like warfarin or novel oral anticoagulants (NOACs), are preferred for stroke prevention in AFib due to their superior effectiveness.
snippet_highlighted_words: it is less effective than other anticoagulants and carries a similar risk of bleeding

text_blocks.snippet: Here's why aspirin is not the best choice for AFib:

list.title: Lower Effectiveness:
list.snippet: Studies show that aspirin is less effective at preventing strokes in AFib patients compared to anticoagulants like warfarin or NOACs.

list.title: Similar Bleeding Risk:
list.snippet: Aspirin carries a risk of bleeding, similar to some NOACs.

list.title: Superior Alternatives:
list.snippet: Oral anticoagulants have demonstrated greater efficacy in reducing stroke risk associated with AFib, making them the preferred treatment option.

list.title: Not Recommended for Most AFib Patients:
list.snippet: For most patients with AFib, aspirin is not the first-line treatment for stroke prevention due to the aforementioned reasons, according to Atrial Fibrillation Centers of America.
